editorial:
Imagine a world where bank robbers care more about their follower count than the actual money. That is exactly what you get here. You follow a crew of young thieves who livestream their crimes to millions of people, turning high-stakes robberies into a viral game. It feels like a mix of a heist movie and a social media nightmare. You will love the tension as they try to stay one step ahead of a grumpy old-school FBI agent and a tech genius who can track their every move. The vibe is high-energy and feels very modern, making you wonder if anyone in the real world is actually this reckless for likes.

Everything about the action is top-notch because David Leitch knows how to film a fight scene. The pacing never lets up, though some of the dialogue feels a bit too cheesy at times. If you enjoy movies that keep you guessing with smart twists, you need to see this.
endingExplained: In the final act, you find out the software engineer was actually working with the robbers to skim money off the top. During the big finale, the FBI agent catches them, but the crew uses a fake livestream to trick the police into raiding the wrong building. Most of the crew escapes with the loot, but the leader gets arrested after his own phone betrays his location. It ends with a funny shot of the agent finally learning how to use a smartphone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves high-tech heists and fast action.
